conventions.convention: Coordinate averages use the finite product sigma-algebra and product probability, without completion; exceptional nonintegrable sections receive zero. P_full f=f and P_empty f=E f as L2 classes.
ANOVA components are f_u=sum over v⊆u of (-1)^(|u|-|v|) P_v f, including f_empty=E f.
Independent-input Sobol indices divide singleton or containing-coordinate ANOVA variance sums by V only when V>0; normalized indices are undefined when V=0.
Under AC, dependent-input Shapley effects average marginal gains of v(S)=Var(E[Y|sigma(X_j:j∈S)]) over uniform permutations and normalize by known V>0.
The first-order hybrid retains X_i and replaces all other coordinates; the total-effect hybrid replaces only X_i.

Pick-freeze rows use six mutually independent input vectors; different rows are independent. A zero sample-mean denominator returns a status without indices; positive denominators produce unclipped ratios and sample-covariance plug-in MCSE.

Support-grouped infinite coefficient formulas assume Countable Choice and a complete real orthonormal tensor family containing the constant mode. Finite polynomial orthogonality alone supplies no completeness.

The derivative bound assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, a product-measurable representative with almost-everywhere absolutely continuous coordinate sections, square-integrable derivative, positive interval length, and positive output variance.

load_bearing.statement: Each P_J is a well-defined self-adjoint contraction on real L2(μ), P_J²=P_J, and P_J P_K=P_(J∩K) for all J,K⊆[d].

For finite independent product inputs and real f∈L2, f is the sum of its ANOVA components in L2; each component depends only on its indexed coordinates, nonempty components are centered in each own coordinate, distinct components are orthogonal, and Var(f) is the sum of their nonempty squared norms.

For f∈L2 under a finite product law and an independent copy X', the covariance of f(X) with f(X_i,X'_-i) is V_{i}; half the expected squared difference between f(X) and f(X_-i,X'_i) is the sum of V_u over u containing i.

Assume AC and the positive-variance hypotheses of the Shapley definition. The variance game is monotone with endpoints 0 and V and range [0,V]; every Shapley effect is nonnegative and their sum is one. Exact permutation enumeration terminates with at most 2d d! coalition-value calls and returns these effects.
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For an absolutely continuous real g on an interval of length L>0 with g'∈L2, and uniform U on that interval, Var(g(U))≤(L²/π²) E|g'(U)|².

concerns.concern: Fact F1 says that “the ratio is returned when D>0,” immediately after defining the single-row denominator D. The algorithm instead returns when the sample mean of the row denominators is positive. The subsequent two-row proof correctly uses K>0 and bar D=K/4, so this is a notation error in the fact rather than a defect in the 5/6 calculation.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and its finite-product input definition, positive-moment Gram lemma, and finite tensor-basis definition against the consuming page and polynomial-chaos example. The supplier asserts finite orthogonality without general completeness. The consumer preserves that limitation, separately assumes completeness for infinite coefficient formulas, and proves completeness directly for its four-point example.
